claims.text: The FDA alprazolam label says co-use with opioids, the class containing dihydrocodeine, may cause profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death.
claims.quote: Concomitant use of benzodiazepines, including alprazolam, and opioids may result in profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death.

claims.text: The French dihydrocodeine label says opioid-benzodiazepine co-use increases sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death through additive CNS depression.
claims.quote: L’utilisation concomitante d’opioïdes avec des médicaments sédatifs tels que les benzodiazépines ou les médicaments apparentés augmente le risque de sédation, de dépression respiratoire, de coma et de décès en raison d’un effet dépresseur additif sur le système nerveux central.
claims.quoteEnglish: Concomitant use of opioids with sedative medicines such as benzodiazepines or related medicines increases the risk of sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death because of an additive depressant effect on the central nervous system.

headline.text: The FDA alprazolam label flags profound sedation and respiratory depression with opioids, the class containing dihydrocodeine.

reported.text: The French dihydrocodeine label also warns about opioid-benzodiazepine co-use; alprazolam is a benzodiazepine.

mechanism.text: The French label attributes the increased risk to additive CNS depression.

gaps.text: The packet contains no controlled human study specifically testing alprazolam with dihydrocodeine.
